clusters.name: Your grandfather Amos's death, 1989–1990
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Amos's death in July 1989, within the following months: your mother's anxiety rising as she lay awake over money in March 1988, then in May 1988 she and your father stopped talking about money; your brother's grades fell in November 1989; and your mother's anxiety eased once she returned to work in March 1990. The shifts in money worry and distance between your parents came first, then the death, then your brother's functioning fell, and your mother's anxiety lifted as she moved back into work—a sequence of movements among these three across more than a year.

clusters.name: Your mother Della told she had breast cancer, 1995–1996
clusters.reason: Around your mother Della's diagnosis of breast cancer in February 1995: you developed migraines that kept you in bed starting in March 1994, called your brother most nights from April 1994, then in June 1995 you stopped returning his calls, and by February 1996 you stopped calling home. Your own symptom rose and your moves toward and away from your brother bookend the months when your mother's diagnosis arrived—every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then, but the pattern of moves toward your brother and then away, with your symptom rising underneath, falls tight around your mother's illness and holds together as your reaction to it.
